rationale: Anytype documents a localhost API bundled with the desktop app, a versioned OpenAPI spec, and an official MCP server for AI assistants. A CLI runs Anytype as a headless server for automation, and an agents skill lets Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools read, search and modify Objects, including bulk edits. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that headless read/write works as documented (all evidence is first-party, and API v2 is still pre-release).

A probe confirms a live llms.txt at doc.anytype.io (HTTP 200) indexing the docs as raw .md pages, which an agent can ingest directly. Agent-oriented material is also present: an agents skill toolkit for Claude Code, Cursor and similar tools, an AGENTS.md in the main repo, and a machine-readable OpenAPI spec on the developer portal. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of agents actually using these docs, and no evidence of an llms.txt or llms-full.txt for the developer/API portal.

Anytype has no documented built-in AI that generates insights or suggestions inside the app. AI can only reach your data through external assistants such as Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot, connected via the official MCP server, the local API, or the Agents skill, which let those tools read, search and modify Objects. Queries and the Graph are rule-based, not AI. Missing for 10: native in-product AI insights or suggestions, any documented insight or suggestion feature even via integrations, and hands-on corroboration.

Anytype has no native automation engine, but it offers building blocks: a headless CLI server explicitly "for automation and scripting", a local API, an official MCP server, and an agents skill that lets external agent tools run scripts for bulk and repetitive tasks. Autonomous background automation therefore depends on external agents, schedulers or custom scripts. Missing for 10: built-in automation/trigger/scheduling features, documented autonomous background workflows inside Anytype, independent or hands-on corroboration.

Delegating to an AI assistant is a fair axis for a knowledge-management app like Anytype, but the evidence describes no assistant built into the product. What it does show is external agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot) acting on Anytype data through the local API, an MCP server and an agents skill. Its chat features are messaging between people, not an AI assistant, and the GitHub 'AI Agents (see AGENTS.md)' line is too vague to show an in-app assistant. Delegation to external tools does not meet the 'built-in' requirement of this story.

Anytype's developer portal says the Anytype CLI can run Anytype as a headless server for automation and scripting, which directly matches the story. The localhost API and the scripting-oriented agents skill support programmatic use against that server, but this rests on a single short first-party announcement with no detail on setup or CI use. Missing for 10: detailed CLI/headless setup docs, explicit CI pipeline guidance or examples (e.g. a containerized headless client), authentication handling for non-interactive environments, independent or hands-on corroboration.

The evidence shows only the reverse direction: an official MCP server and an agents skill that let external AI assistants such as Claude Code or Cursor read and modify Anytype data. Nothing shows Anytype itself acting as an MCP client that connects to external MCP servers and uses their tools. Being a server or an integration target does not satisfy this client-side story.

Anytype's developer portal has a featured MCP page describing an official server that lets AI assistants interact with the Anytype API through natural language, and a probe confirmed the page exists. The server sits on top of the local API bundled with the desktop app. Missing for 10: detail on the server's tools and setup steps, independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting an agent, and clarity on whether it works without the desktop app running.

Anytype documents an official MCP server that lets AI assistants interact with its API through natural language. Its open-source agents skill lets tools like Claude Code, Cursor or Copilot read, search and modify Objects and run bulk edits. Natural-language operation therefore works only through a third-party AI assistant, not natively in the app. Missing for 10: a built-in natural-language command interface, hands-on or independent corroboration that NL operation works reliably, and documentation of which product actions can be driven this way.

The official developer portal announces an Anytype CLI that runs Anytype as a headless server for automation and scripting, which fits the AI-native story. The official agents skill also lets agent tools like Claude Code and Gemini CLI run scripts against Anytype data, reinforcing the scripting workflow. Missing for 10: CLI command reference or install/usage docs, details on agent-oriented features (e.g. structured/JSON output), and independent or hands-on corroboration that the CLI works as described.

Anytype ships a documented local API inside the desktop app, plus a headless CLI server mode for automation. A developer portal publishes a machine-readable OpenAPI spec (openapi-v2.yaml) with full schemas, error responses, dated API versions, and a changelog, and it also offers an official MCP server and an agents toolkit built on that API. The 404s from the OpenAPI probe were on doc.anytype.io, while the spec lives on developers.anytype.io, so they are not a contradiction. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of API use, a written deprecation policy and try-it console, and a stable v2 (currently pre-release); the API is also localhost-only, requiring the desktop app or headless CLI.

Anytype's OpenAPI spec shows the local API uses keys that can be revoked or expire ("Missing, unknown, revoked or expired key"), so per-agent credentials can be issued for MCP or agent-skill access. Nothing in the evidence shows those keys can be scoped to particular spaces, objects, or read-only access, which is the core least-privilege part of the story. Missing for 10: documented per-key scopes or permissions (space/object restriction, read-only vs write), a key issuance and management workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

Anytype offers official programmatic surfaces: a localhost API with a published, versioned OpenAPI spec, a gRPC API, a headless CLI for scripting, an official MCP server, and an open-source agents toolkit that runs scripts against Anytype data. Missing for 10: explicitly documented official SDK packages (e.g., JS/Python client libraries), SDK reference docs, a deprecation policy, and independent hands-on corroboration of building with them.

Anytype exposes a local API, a headless CLI server, an MCP server, and an agents skill. However, the docs explicitly state that no written deprecation policy page is published, so half of the story is unmet. Anytype's first-party agents skill says an agent can run scripts against your Anytype data to handle bulk edits, transformations, and repetitive tasks. However, bulk work depends on scripting through an external agent tool (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) looping over the API, not on a native multi-item operation. Missing for 10: a documented native batch/bulk endpoint or in-app multi-select bulk edit, concrete docs or examples of bulk operations, and independent hands-on corroboration.

The evidence pack shows no event-triggered rules engine, webhooks, or event subscriptions in Anytype. It documents only adjacent capabilities: a local API, a headless CLI for scripting, and an agent skill for running bulk-edit scripts, all of which require external tooling and include no trigger mechanism. Queries that auto-update and templates applied to new Objects are not user-defined rules that fire actions on events.

The evidence shows a local API, a headless CLI for automation and scripting, and an agents skill that runs scripts for bulk or repetitive tasks. None of it mentions scheduling, triggers, or recurring execution of jobs or workflows within Anytype. Any recurring automation would rest entirely on external tooling that the evidence never describes.

Automation is a fair axis for Anytype, which documents a local API, a headless CLI for scripting, and an agents skill that runs scripts against your data. However, nothing in the evidence shows a way to version, review, or roll back those automations. The dated API releases describe versions of the API itself, not of a user's automations, so they don't count here.

Anytype documents linking between Objects as the basis of a connected knowledge base, says you can trace how ideas relate and see what connects to a project, and offers a live Graph of how Objects connect. That covers basic inter-note linking and a visual view of connections only. Nothing in the evidence shows the specific researcher workflow of wiki-style links with in-context backlinks and unlinked mentions. Missing for 10: documented [[wiki-style]] link syntax, a backlinks panel showing linking context, unlinked-mention detection, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

Block-level referencing or transclusion is a fair axis for a block-based note-taking app like Anytype. The pack only documents object-level linking and the graph (anytype-docs-28, anytype-docs-40, anytype-docs-9) and generic composable blocks. Nothing shows referencing or embedding an individual block or section from another note and keeping it in sync.

The evidence shows no built-in AI assistant in Anytype. AI grounded in your notes is only possible by connecting external assistants through the official MCP server, the localhost-only offline API, or the Agents Skill, which gives assistants like Claude Code or Cursor a 'safe way to read, search, and modify Objects'. Revocable API keys and local-only operation provide some control over what the AI can access. Missing for 10: a native in-app AI assistant, documented in-app Q&A/summarize/draft features, granular per-space or per-object controls over AI data visibility, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

A plugin catalog is a fair axis for a note-taking and knowledge app, so the story applies. The evidence shows only extensibility through a local API, a gRPC API, an MCP server, a CLI and an agents skill. Nothing shows an in-app catalog or marketplace of community plugins that users can browse and install.

Daily notes are a fair axis for a note-taking and knowledge-base app like Anytype. The pack shows reusable Templates and a calendar block type, but no evidence of automatically generated per-day notes, template pre-fill for them, or a daily note as the default landing page. Templates alone do not deliver the story's core of automatic daily creation and landing.

Anytype's docs say its own infrastructure handles background syncing and backups automatically [anytype-docs-42], and that content lives in an encrypted Vault that "not even Anytype can see" [anytype-docs-31, anytype-docs-43, anytype-docs-44, anytype-docs-27]. Apps exist for macOS, Windows, Linux, iOS and Android [anytype-docs-54], and hands-on users report that cross-device sync "worked great" and describe the protocol as E2E encrypted [anytype-comm-8, anytype-comm-5, anytype-comm-3]. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of the encryption and key model behind the vendor-can't-read claim (the pack has only short claims), and full on-device encryption of indexes.

The self-host guide describes exporting all channels and re-importing them into a new identity, which covers whole-knowledge-base export. The localhost API adds a programmatic path to the data. Missing for 10: documentation of what Markdown export preserves (properties, relations, database views, files), clarity on whether Any-Block is an open or documented format, and independent or hands-on corroboration that a full export works for leaving the product.

Queries let you define criteria and get an instantly updated View of matching Objects. The docs describe the app as offline-first, with all content stored locally and the local API running fully offline. The agents toolkit can also search Objects. However, the evidence never explicitly documents full-text search across note bodies in the app, or filtering by tags, properties, or paths. Missing for 10: explicit full-text content search documentation, documented tag/property filter operators, path/folder-based filtering, independent hands-on confirmation of search speed and offline search.

Anytype documents a Graph view described as a live, visual map of every Object in a Channel and how they connect, and its linking docs describe tracing how ideas relate. Missing for 10: evidence of graph filtering (by type, tag, or relation), detail on interactive navigation within the graph, independent or hands-on corroboration of the graph view.

Anytype documents a general import feature and a Markdown import path through its Obsidian migration guide (Channel Settings → Import → Obsidian), which creates one object per Markdown file. However, the store is an encrypted, app-specific format (the team says data is encrypted at rest), so reading notes without the app requires exporting to Markdown or Any-Block rather than opening plain local files. Missing for 10: notes stored as plain files directly readable without the app, independent hands-on corroboration of offline behavior.

Missing for 10: documented mobile feature parity for search, linking, and capture workflows (e.g., share-sheet/quick capture), and hands-on evidence of power-user mobile use rather than basic note-taking.

Anytype's first-party docs describe Templates as saved, reusable page layouts that form the base for every new Object created afterwards, and custom Types let you model recurring kinds of notes. Nothing in the pack shows dynamic variables such as date or title being filled in when a template is applied, which the story explicitly asks for. Missing for 10: template variables/placeholders (date, title) auto-filled on creation, detail on per-Type default template selection, independent or hands-on corroboration.

Anytype's docs say you can export content at any time [anytype-docs-20] and offer Markdown as an export format alongside Any-Block [anytype-docs-11].
